title: High-dimensional functional phenotyping of preclinical human CAR T cells using mass cytometry
protocol: Collect fresh human whole blood sample from an adult healthy donor in tubes containing an anti-coagulant.
Keep the collected blood sample overnight (16–18 h) at room temperature on a rocker.
Dilute the peripheral blood sample 1:2 in PBS and invert gently.
Aliquot 15 mL of Ficoll-PaqueTM PLUS density gradient medium into new 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Slowly layer the diluted peripheral blood sample onto the Ficoll-PaqueTM PLUS medium by pipetting it down the side of the Falcon tube.
Layer the diluted blood sample on top of the Ficoll-PaqueTM PLUS medium in a 50 mL Falcon tube at a 45° angle without mixing.
Centrifuge the Falcon tube containing the diluted blood and Ficoll-PaqueTM PLUS medium at 700×g for 20 minutes at room temperature with the brake turned off.
Gently handle the tubes after centrifugation to avoid disrupting the density gradient formed.
Aspirate and discard most of the top layer, approximately two-thirds of it, without disturbing the mononuclear cell layer.
Prepare two 50 mL Falcon tubes for PBMC isolation.
Aspirate the mononuclear layer with a Pasteur pipette and transfer it to new 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Avoid aspirating the underlying Ficoll-PaqueTM PLUS medium while harvesting the mononuclear layer.
Top up the Falcon tubes containing harvested PBMCs with PBS, invert gently, and centrifuge at 220×g for 5 minutes.
Repeat washing step for a total of two washes.
Discard supernatant without disturbing the PBMC pellet.
Resuspend PBMCs in 10 mL of TexMACSTM medium.
Take an aliquot of resuspended cells and count them using a hematology automated analyser.
Record WBC and lymphocyte counts.
Proceed with the next step “activation of T cells from human PBMCs”.
Stratify diluted peripheral blood on top of Ficoll-PaqueTM PLUS medium at a 45° angle.
Dilute isolated PBMCs to 1 × 10^6 WBCs/mL with TexMACSTM medium.
Vortex CTSTM DynabeadsTM CD3/CD28 for more than 30 seconds to resuspend them.
Wash CTSTM DynabeadsTM CD3/CD28.
Take an aliquot of CTSTM DynabeadsTM CD3/CD28 at a ratio of 7.5 μL beads per million lymphocytes and mix it with an equal volume of TexMACSTM medium in a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Vortex the 15 mL Falcon tube.
Place the 15 mL Falcon tube on a DynaMagTM-15 Magnet for 1 minute.
Aspirate off the supernatant from the magnetized tube.
Resuspend the washed beads in TexMACSTM medium at a volume of 7.5 μL per million lymphocytes.
Add washed CTSTM DynabeadsTM CD3/CD28 to isolated PBMCs.
Mix PBMCs with the DynabeadsTM carefully.
Plate the mixture into a Flask at a concentration of 1 × 106 WBCs/mL.
Gently mix the Flask content for 10 min on a rocker or manually every 2 min.
Incubate the Flask at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Transduce T cells from human PBMCs with a lentiviral vector expressing an anti-CD19 FMC63-based CAR construct.
Harvest the cell:bead mixture into two pre-labeled 50 mL Falcon tubes after 17–24 hours.
Wash the Flask twice with CliniMACS® PBS/EDTA buffer to improve cell recovery.
Centrifuge the 50 mL Falcon tubes containing the cell:bead mixture at 220×g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant from the centrifuged tubes.
Resuspend the cell:bead mixture in 10 mL of TexMACSTM medium.
Count the resuspended cells using the same instrument as on day 1 to maintain consistency.
Record the WBC and lymphocyte counts.
Resuspend the cell:bead mixture in TexMACSTM medium at a concentration of 1 × 10^6 WBCs/mL.
Aliquot 500 μL of cell:bead mixture per well into a 24-well plate.
Add the lentiviral supernatant to the cells at a multiplicity of infection (MOIs) between 1–10.
Mix well.
Incubate the plate at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Top up with TexMACSTM medium each well containing transduced beads-activated T-cells to augment T cell expansion.
Spin down the plate at 220×g for 5 min.
Aspirate no more than half of the supernatant without perturbing the cells.
Add fresh TexMACSTM medium into each well.
Daily check the cell culture to assess expansion, activation and transduction level.
Monitor T cell cluster formation as a hallmark of activation.
Assess mCherry expression as a proxy for CAR expression.
Harvest the cell:bead mixture in a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Wash the wells with PBS to improve cell recovery.
Top up the 50 mL Falcon tube with PBS.
Centrifuge the 50 mL Falcon tube at 220×g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 13 mL of TexMACSTM medium.
Move the cells into a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Remove DynabeadsTM from the cell culture using a magnet.
Aspirate the cell content without perturbing the beads.
Transfer the cells into a new 15 mL Falcon tube.
Count the cells using an automated cell counter and record their concentration and viability.
Seed the cells in TexMACSTM medium at a concentration of 1 × 10^6/mL.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Optional: Leave the cells resting for 1 day after bead-removal to maximize CAR-dependent response and minimize DynabeadsTM-driven intracellular signaling response detected by mass cytometry.
Count the NALM6 and the CAR T cells.
Resuspend each of them to a concentration of 1 million/mL in TexMACSTM medium.
Irradiate NALM6 cells with 40 Gy using a 137 Cesium radioactive source.
Alternatives: Instead of irradiating the target cells, treat them with Mitomycin C before co-culture.
Aliquot CAR T cells in 96-, 24-, or 12-well plates according to the number of cells.
Add NALM6 in a 1:1 ratio with CAR T cells (in the stimulated condition).
Add an equal volume of TexMACSTM medium to CAR T cells (in the unstimulated condition).
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Proceed with sample preparation for mass cytometry analysis.
Stimulate at least 0.2–0.5 × 10^6 CAR T cells in this step for mass cytometry phenotyping.
Analyze the cells by mass cytometry 24 hours post antigen-stimulation.
Consider varying the stimulation period from a few minutes to days based on user needs.
If interested in CAR T cell exhaustion, perform repeated antigen stimulation rounds.
Add wild-type cell line in the unstimulated condition if using genetically engineered cell lines expressing target antigens.
Treat unstimulated and stimulated samples with Brefeldin A to inhibit endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi protein transport.
Stain the samples with Cell-IDTM 127 IdU to incorporate thymidine analogue into DNA during S-phase for proliferating cell identification.
Fix the samples to preserve their biochemical and molecular state.
Add Brefeldin A Solution to unstimulated and stimulated samples to a final concentration of 1× (1:1,000 dilution).
Mix gently by pipetting.
Incubate for 4 h at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Dilute Cell-IDTM 127 IdU in unstimulated and stimulated samples after 3 h 30 min to a final concentration of 50 μM (1:1,000 dilution).
Mix gently by pipetting.
Incubate for 30 min at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Dilute 16% formaldehyde in PBS to prepare 1.6% FA (1:10 dilution) during the incubation period.
Prepare fresh 1.6% formaldehyde by mixing 5 mL of 16% FA with 45 mL of PBS for four experimental conditions.
Filter the stock FA before diluting, if necessary.
Harvest cells into pre-labeled individual 15 mL Falcon tubes after the end of incubation.
Wash each well with 200 μL of Maxpar® PBS to collect any residual cell.
Centrifuge the 15 mL Falcon tubes at 220×g for 5 min at room temperature.
Fix cells with 1 mL of freshly prepared 1.6% formaldehyde (FA) solution.
Gently mix by vortexing.
Incubate for 7 minutes at room temperature.
Wash cells with 2 mL of Maxpar® Cell Staining Buffer (CSB).
Centrifuge at 1,200×g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in residual volume by gentle pipetting or vortexing.
Repeat wash step using 2 mL of CSB.
Centrifuge at 1,200×g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Gently resuspend cells in the residual volume.
After the second wash, aspirate the supernatant.
Do not resuspend the cell pellet to preserve cell integrity.
Leave the pelleted cells in the residual Maxpar® CSB volume (approximately 200 μL).
Store the cell pellets in 15 mL Falcon tubes at 4°C.
Pause point: Cells can be stored in FA at 4°C for up to one week (7–10 days).
Stain unstimulated and stimulated fixed samples with cisplatin (Cell-IDTM Cisplatin).
Detect its signal in the 195/194Pt channel of CyTOF® mass cytometer.
Distinguish between live (cisplatin low) and dead (cisplatin high) cells.
Reconstitute Cell-IDTM Cisplatin immediately before use at room temperature.
Count samples in the residual volume without using viability dye.
Centrifuge cells at 1,200×g for 5 min at room temperature.
Resuspend cell pellets in 500 μL of Maxpar® PBS.
Dilute Cell-IDTM Cisplatin 1:5,000 in Maxpar® PBS to achieve a cisplatin concentration of 1 μM.
Aliquot 500 μL of the 1 μM cisplatin solution into 500 μL of cells, achieving a final cisplatin concentration of 0.5 μM.
Resuspend the cell mixture carefully.
Incubate for 1 min on a rocker at room temperature.
Quench the cisplatin by adding 5 mL of Maxpar® CSB to each 15 mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 1,200×g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant and gently vortex to resuspend the cell pellet.
Add 4 mL of Maxpar® PBS to wash cells.
Centrifuge at 1,200×g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant and gently vortex to resuspend the cell pellet.
Dilute 10× Barcode Perm Buffer 1:10 in Maxpar® PBS.
Aliquot 1 mL of 1× Barcode Perm Buffer into each sample and centrifuge at 1,200×g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and repeat the wash.
Resuspend each pellet in 800 μL of 1× Barcode Perm Buffer.
Equilibrate one set of 4 barcodes at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Assign a unique barcode to each sample and record it.
Quickly spin the barcode tubes using a mini microfuge.
Add 100 μL of 1× Barcode Perm Buffer to each barcode, gently resuspend, and transfer them to the assigned samples.
Gently vortex the samples and incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature on a rocker.
Invert the sample tubes twice every 10 minutes during incubation.
Centrifuge the barcoded samples at 1,200×g for 5 minutes, discard the supernatant, and gently vortex.
Add 2 mL of Maxpar® CSB to the barcoded samples and centrifuge them at 1,200×g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and repeat the wash.
Resuspend each barcoded cell pellet in 200 μL of Maxpar® CSB.
Centrifuge the barcoded samples at 1,200×g for 5 minutes.
Store the barcoded samples as cell pellets at 4°C without resuspending them or removing the supernatant.
Pool together different conditions per each donor into a single tube if more than one donor is present in the experiment.
Incubate the multiplexed sample with Fc receptor blocking solution (Human TruStain FcXTM) to reduce unspecific antibody binding.
Stain the multiplexed sample with an antibody mix for surface antigens.
Pool all barcoded samples from one single donor into a pre-labeled 15 mL Falcon tube.
Wash barcoded samples if stored for longer than one month to prevent cross-contamination due to barcode leakage.
Resuspend pooled cells in the 15 mL Falcon tube and count them without using a viability dye.
Centrifuge the 15 mL Falcon tube at 1,200×g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Dilute Human TruStain FcXTM 1:20 in Maxpar® CSB following the manufacturer’s recommendations.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 50 μL of diluted Human TruStain FcXTM, mix well.
Incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Vortex and quickly spin (110×g for 30 seconds) each antibody before preparing the surface antibody mix.
Aliquot 50 μL of surface antibody mix into the multiplexed sample.
Gently mix the combined solution.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature.
Vortex the multiplexed sample every 10 min during incubation.
Add 2 mL of Maxpar® CSB to the multiplexed sample.
Centrifuge at 1,000×g for 7 min.
Aspirate off the supernatant.
Pulse vortex the multiplexed sample to disaggregate the cell pellet.
Prepare the Foxp3 Fixation/Permeabilization solution by diluting the Fixation/Permeabilization Concentrate 1:4 into the eBioscienceTM Fixation/Permeabilization Diluent.
Aliquot 1 mL of Foxp3 Fixation/Permeabilization solution to the multiplexed sample and pulse vortex.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature in the dark.
Dilute the 10× Permeabilization Buffer (Perm Buffer) 1:10 into Maxpar® Water (final concentration 1×).
Vortex each antibody before preparing the mix.
Aliquot 2 mL of 1× Perm Buffer to the multiplexed sample and centrifuge at 1,000×g for 7 min at room temperature.
Aspirate off the supernatant and repeat step.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 50 μL of 1× Perm Buffer.
Aliquot 50 μL of cytoplasmic antibody mix into the multiplexed sample (total staining volume 100 μL).
Gently vortex and incubate for 30 min at room temperature.
Gently vortex the multiplexed sample every 10 min to prevent cell clumping.
Wash the multiplexed sample by adding 2 mL of 1× Perm Buffer.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,000×g for 7 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate off the supernatant.
Prepare 50% Methanol in Maxpar® PBS and store it at −20°C.
Store an aliquot of Maxpar® CSB at 4°C.
Wash the cells with 2 mL of Maxpar® CSB.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,000×g for 7 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in the residual volume by gently vortexing.
Fix the multiplexed sample in ice-cold 50% Methanol.
Stain the fixed sample for phosphoprotein and nuclear protein detection.
Incubate the multiplexed sample on ice for 1 min.
Aliquot 1 mL of ice-cold 50% Methanol to the multiplexed sample, gently mix and incubate for 10 min on ice.
Vortex and quickly spin each antibody before preparing the mix at 110×g for 30 sec.
Add 2 mL of ice-cold Maxpar® CSB to the multiplexed sample and centrifuge it at 1,000×g for 7 min.
Discard the supernatant and repeat step 113.
Gently vortex to resuspend the cells in the residual volume (approximately 50 μL).
Add 50 μL of phosphoprotein and nuclear antibody mix to the cells (total staining volume 100 μL).
Mix well and incubate for 30 min on ice.
During the incubation, gently vortex the multiplexed sample every 10 min to prevent cell clumps.
Add 2 mL of ice-cold Maxpar® CSB to the multiplexed sample and centrifuge it at 1,000×g for 7 min.
Discard the supernatant and repeat step 117.
Gently vortex to resuspend the cells in the residual volume.
Proceed with cell fixation and DNA staining with Cell-ID™ Intercalator-Ir.
Dilute 16% formaldehyde in PBS (1:10 dilution) to make 1.6% FA.
Aliquot 1 mL of freshly prepared 1.6% FA into the tube after vortexing it.
Gently vortex to mix well.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature on a rocker.
Equilibrate the Cell-IDTM Intercalator-Ir at room temperature during incubation.
Wash the sample with 1 mL of Maxpar® CSB and centrifuge it at 1,000×g for 7 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant and gently vortex to resuspend the cells in the residual volume.
Stain the sample with Cell-IDTM Intercalator-Ir.
Dilute Cell-IDTM Intercalator-Ir 1:1,000 with Maxpar® Fix and Perm buffer (final concentration 125 nM).
Vortex the intercalator solution.
Aliquot 1 mL of intercalator solution into the sample and vortex.
Incubate overnight at 4°C for 16–18 hours.
Optionally, incubate the sample with intercalator solution for 1 hour at room temperature.
Proceed to "Sample acquisition" step the following day.
Store samples in intercalator solution at 4°C for up to 48 hours if necessary.
Add 2 mL of Maxpar® Cell Acquisition Solution (CAS) to the multiplexed sample.
Centrifuge at 1,200×g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in the residual volume by vortexing.
Repeat step: Add 2 mL of CAS and centrifuge at 1,200×g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate off the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of CAS.
Take an aliquot of resuspended cells for counting.
Dilute the cells in CAS to a concentration of 0.5–1×10^6/mL if needed.
Carefully mix the EQTM Four Element Calibration Beads.
Add the EQTM Four Element Calibration Beads to the sample at a 1:5 bead:cell ratio.
Filter the sample into a polypropylene FACS tube using a 35 μm cell strainer cap.
Vortex the filtered sample immediately before acquisition.
Acquire the sample for 10,000 seconds at a flow rate of less than 600 events per second.
Normalize the acquired FCS files against the EQTM Four Element Calibration Beads.
Debarcode the normalized FCS files using Fluidigm CyTOF Software.
